title: Seacliff - search relevance & rerank hosted API walkthrough
summary: Redwood hosted embeddings + rerank demo oriented around Seacliff's newsroom search use case. Covered embedding vectors, reranker endpoint, Console quickstart, Optimize recommendations (batching / quantization), and security/residency questions. Agreed to run a 2-week pilot + benchmark, Redwood to send pricing, security docs, and a pilot template.
action_items: Maya: send hosted vs dedicated pricing and recommended pilot scope by 2026-08-06
Jordan: share sample benchmark script and terraform snippet for seeding test data by 2026-08-07
Priya: provide top 500 user queries and success metric definition by 2026-08-10
next_steps: Redwood to send pricing and security pack
Schedule technical deep dive with infra (VPC/private) if pilot looks good
Start 2-week hosted pilot focusing on search rerank using 100k docs
meeting_header: Date: 2026-08-04 | Time: 15:00 PDT | Duration: ~48m | Link: (zoom) | Attendees: Maya Khan (Redwood AE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood Product), Priya Singh (Seacliff Head of Search), Tom Alvarez (Seacliff Eng Manager), Liam O'Rourke (Seacliff Data Scientist)
transcript:
[00:00:00] Maya Khan: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll kick off in a sec. uh quick check audio?
[00:00:07] Priya Singh: can you hear me, yes good morning from nyc.
[00:00:12] Jordan Lee: yep loud and clear, jordan from redwood here, i'll lead the product walkthrough after maya sets context.
[00:00:20] Maya Khan: great, goal for today: show our hosted embeddings + reranking endpoints and the console experience, and talk about an initial pilot for newsroom search relevance. should be about 40 to 50 minutes and then q&a.
[00:00:34] Tom Alvarez: sounds good. our main ask — speed up search relevance for 1st page results and reduce manual tuning. latency is a concern, we target sub 120ms for top results.
[00:00:45] Maya Khan: totally. we usually look at tradeoffs: hosted api can hit low latencies for embeddings+rerank on our verified models, and if needed we discuss dedicated pools later.
[00:00:00] Jordan Lee: alright i'll share my screen — pulling up the console, apologies if the screen share lags on your side.
[00:01:05] [screen share] Jordan Lee: this is the redwood console, main nav on left. quick demo order: 1) embeddings endpoint, 2) search + retrieval pattern, 3) reranker endpoint with scoring, 4) optimize suggestions for batching/kv, and 5) how to run a quick benchmark from the UI or api.
[00:01:28] Liam O'Rourke: quick question: which embedding model do you recommend for short news snippets versus full article content?
[00:01:34] Jordan Lee: good one — for shorter snippets we often recommend redwood-sim-sml-001 (higher throughput), for long-form article vectors use redwood-sem-long-002. both are in the model catalog, with perf profiles. note: model names sometimes get garbled in transcripts, but the console shows exact tags.
[00:01:54] Priya Singh: and what about vector dimension? we currently run a 768 dim model with our old pipeline.
[00:02:01] Jordan Lee: you can pick dims, but our defaults are 768 and 1024 depending on model. 768 is a fine starting point and will keep storage/costs lower.
[00:02:12] [00:02:12] Tom Alvarez: cost concern — how are embeddings billed? token or per-request?
[00:02:19] Maya Khan: hosted embeddings are billed per-embedding call (per 1k units) — i'll include an explicit pricing sheet after the call. we also give guidance in Optimize to reduce calls with caching and batching.
[00:02:32] Jordan Lee: jumping to the reranker: typical flow is retrieve top N with vector similarity (faiss or your vector DB), then call our reranker endpoint to rescore and reorder top 50 or top 20. reranker accepts original query, candidate docs, and returns a score + optional structured explanation.
[00:02:55] Priya Singh: structured explanation as in why it moved something up? that could be super helpful for editors.
[00:03:01] Jordan Lee: yes, we have an explainability field — it's not perfect LLM explainable but gives feature-level signals like recency, semantic match, and passage coverage. sometimes the transcript will say k v cash or kv cache, but it's the KV cache in the runtime that helps short-circuit recompute.
[00:03:20] [00:03:20] Liam O'Rourke: latency again — if we do retrieve top 100 then rerank, what's typical end-to-end latency hosted?
[00:03:27] Jordan Lee: depends on model and candidates. for a light reranker model we see median rerank latencies ~40-80ms per call at small scale; end-to-end (retrieve + rerank + post-processing) typically under 150ms for top-20 with our hosted tier. we'll need to benchmark with your payload sizes.
[00:03:45] Samir Patel: also Optimize will recommend batching strategies and quantization for model reductions. for example, per your query volume we might suggest quantized reranker builds that cut cost by ~40% while adding maybe 10-20ms.
[00:03:58] Tom Alvarez: hmm 10-20ms added could be okay if we save costs. how does fallback work if the hosted capacity is saturated?
[00:04:08] Maya Khan: we support smart routing and fallback — the policy can route to cheaper model variants or to a dedicated pool if configured. for hosted customers we provide auto-fallback to compatible lower-cost variants. we'll include examples in the policy doc.
[00:04:23] Priya Singh: anything to consider for PII or embargoed content? we have articles under embargo and some internal docs.
[00:04:31] Maya Khan: yes — hosted API has configurable data retention and optional private deployment. for embargoed content most customers use dedicated or private to keep control. we have KMS integrations and audit logs — i'll attach SOC2/ISO pack.
[00:04:45] [00:04:45] Jordan Lee: going back to live demo — i'll show a small rerank call.
[00:04:51] [screen activity] Jordan Lee: here is a sample request: payload includes query string, candidate array with id/title/snippet, and metadata. response: score and optional explanation. sample: 
{query: "climate policy updates", candidates: [{id: "d1", snippet: "..."}, {id: "d2", snippet: "..."}], top_k: 5} — our snippet in the console has curl/py examples and SDK snippets.
[00:05:20] Liam O'Rourke: is there streaming for rerank or only full response?
[00:05:24] Jordan Lee: rerank is full response today — streaming is for generative endpoints.
[00:05:28] Priya Singh: can the reranker be used for reordering sections within an article, or just document-level?
[00:05:34] Jordan Lee: both — you can provide passage-level candidates and rerank them, we typically return a score per candidate so you can reorder sections. some folks call it passage reranking.
[00:05:46] [00:05:46] Tom Alvarez: our infra team asked about VPC and private control plane, is that supported on hosted pilots?
[00:05:53] Maya Khan: hosted pilots run on Redwood's shared control plane but you can request a private data path or dedicated capacity for pilots if needed; full VPC/private control plane is part of the Private deployment option. for initial pilots we usually do hosted with strict retention settings.
[00:06:09] Priya Singh: okay, timeline wise we want results in 2-3 weeks, with a small pilot.
[00:06:15] Maya Khan: great — our normal pilots are 2 weeks. we'll scope: seed 100k docs, run top-50 retrieval + rerank, measure ndcg and p@5 and latency.
[00:06:25] [00:06:25] Jordan Lee: i'll now flip to Optimize — this is the Optimize tab where we propose batching, cache and quantization profiles based on your query distribution. here you can preview recommended batch sizes per model and see estimated cost savings.
[00:06:41] Liam O'Rourke: interesting, how do you estimate savings? is it simulation or real run data?
[00:06:46] Samir Patel: it's a mix. we use telemetry from verified profiles and your sample query histogram. it's heuristic but we attach confidence intervals and recommend an A/B with canary to validate.
[00:06:59] Priya Singh: we also integrate with our logging to track click-through and editorial feedback. does Redwood accept feedback signals to retrain reranker or tune thresholds?
[00:07:07] Jordan Lee: yes — you can send human labels or click signals into our retraining pipeline or just use them for offline evaluation. Optimize has a quality monitoring tab where you upload prompt sets and anchor metrics and we alert on regressions.
[00:07:21] [00:07:21] Tom Alvarez: what about the vector DB? we plan to keep our own faiss cluster on prem. do we need to push vectors into your store?
[00:07:29] Jordan Lee: not necessary. typical setup: you compute embeddings (either via Redwood or locally), store vectors in your FAISS, Milvus, or Pinecone, then call Redwood reranker with top N candidates. we also offer managed vector store if you'd prefer a hosted flow.
[00:07:44] Priya Singh: for a hosted pilot we prefer to bring our FAISS and just call rerank api to avoid moving content.
[00:07:50] Maya Khan: that's a common stance and works fine. we'll provide a lightweight benchmark script that does retrieval from your FAISS and calls the reranker — jordan will share that.
[00:07:58] [00:07:58] Liam O'Rourke: any gotchas for multilingual content? we have english plus spanish short summaries.
[00:08:04] Jordan Lee: we have multilingual models, but you should pick a model that supports both or detect language and call appropriate embedder. multilingual rerankers are supported and we have perf profiles per language.
[00:08:17] Priya Singh: regulatory: we have eu users with residency requirements. can you guarantee eu-only processing?
[00:08:24] Maya Khan: yes, we operate regions and can pin processing to eu regions for hosted customers. if you need e2e control, Private deployment is recommended. we'll include data residency options in the security pack.
[00:08:38] [00:08:38] Tom Alvarez: in terms of SLAs — what uptime/latency SLAs do hosted customers get?
[00:08:43] Maya Khan: hosted tier has best-effort with published performance profiles; Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency. for pilots we quote expected latencies based on model choices.
[00:08:55] Jordan Lee: demo time — here's a live rerank response for a newsroom query. note: transcript might show slight mismatches like "dedicate" instead of "dedicated" in auto captions.
[00:09:05] [screen activity/demo] Jordan Lee: sending request... response in 78ms — reordered top docs, explanation includes recency boost for a 2-day-old article and passage coverage.
[00:09:20] Priya Singh: that's within our target. can the explanation surface the exact sentence match?
[00:09:26] Jordan Lee: we give passage-level match scores; we can include the matching token spans on request (be mindful of psr/privacy if exposing text).
[00:09:36] Liam O'Rourke: can we include editorial bias adjustments — e.g., prefer more local sources?
[00:09:42] Samir Patel: yes, reranker accepts metadata signals like source_score and location relevance which are weighted in final scoring; you can adjust via reweighting policy.
[00:09:54] [00:09:54] Tom Alvarez: security again — if we call rerank with candidate snippets, is payload encrypted in transit and at rest?
[00:10:00] Maya Khan: yes TLS in transit, and for hosted we encrypt at rest. if you require HSM-backed keys we support KMS/HSM in Private.
[00:10:10] Priya Singh: ok, sounds good. are there any limits on candidate count for rerank?
[00:10:16] Jordan Lee: practical limits are in the request size; we recommend reranking 20-100 candidates. 100 is okay but will add latency and cost.
[00:10:26] Liam O'Rourke: what about rate limits? we have spikes during breaking news.
[00:10:31] Maya Khan: hosted has rate limits and quotas per account; for spikes we suggest either burst capacity on Dedicated or smart routing to cheaper variants. Optimize can also recommend caching for common queries.
[00:10:44] [00:10:44] Priya Singh: editorial workflow: can editors see reranker explanations in a UI?
[00:10:49] Jordan Lee: yes you can surface the explainability fields into your CMS or use Redwood Console's per-query debug view.
[00:10:59] Tom Alvarez: about billing for the pilot — do you require payment upfront?
[00:11:04] Maya Khan: we'll include pricing options; for pilots we sometimes provide credits, otherwise it's billed on usage. I'll raise this in the follow-up email.
[00:11:14] Priya Singh: great. one more: do you support feature flags to toggle reranker on/off per client?
[00:11:20] Samir Patel: yes, you can set per-route flags and rollout policies, canary and A/B tests.
[00:11:27] [00:11:27] Jordan Lee: jumping to an example optimize suggestion — here we show a recommended batch size of 8 for the embeddings pipeline and a KV cache TTL of 30 minutes for hot queries, estimated cost delta -22%.
[00:11:41] Liam O'Rourke: nice. can we run offline evals against our labeled set?
[00:11:46] Jordan Lee: yes, you upload labeled prompt sets and run the eval tool; it returns ndcg, recall, precision at k, and shows diffs across model versions.
[00:11:58] Priya Singh: can we pin model versions during the pilot so editors see stable behavior?
[00:12:03] Maya Khan: absolutely — you can pin a model version in the deployment config and use rollouts for upgrades.
[00:12:11] [00:12:11] Tom Alvarez: ok this has been useful. i'm going to hand over to priya to ask about editorial acceptance criteria.
[00:12:17] Priya Singh: yes for us success metrics: p@5 improvement > 10% and median rerank latency <150ms. editorial feedback incorporated in retraining pipeline.
[00:12:27] Maya Khan: great. we'll aim to design pilot to measure those.
[00:12:33] Jordan Lee: quick Q&A lightning round, any last technical deep dives needed?
[00:12:38] Tom Alvarez: maybe infra — if pilot hits our latency target we'll talk dedicated pools, otherwise will keep on hosted.
[00:12:45] Maya Khan: noted. i'll follow up with pricing and the security pack; jordan will share the benchmark script and a sample terraform snippet for seeding an example faiss.
[00:12:56] Priya Singh: perfect. when can we get the docs?
[00:13:01] Maya Khan: i'll email everything by friday (2026-08-06).
[00:13:05] Liam O'Rourke: thanks everyone, appreciate the demo.
[00:13:08] Samir Patel: thanks, will be on standby for the pilot setup.
[00:13:12] Maya Khan: ok closing notes: pilot scope and next steps in the summary email, action items assigned. thanks all.
[00:13:20] Priya Singh: thanks, bye.
[00:13:22] Tom Alvarez: bye.
[00:13:24] Jordan Lee: bye.
[00:13:26] [call ended]
notes: Demo showed a live rerank in ~78ms for a newsroom query
Customer prefers keeping FAISS on-prem and calling reranker to avoid moving content
Pilot scoped: 2 weeks, 100k docs, measure ndcg and p@5, latency target <150ms
